newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Court says Belgian road transport fines excessive.
newsitem.headline: Court says Belgian road transport fines excessive.

text.p: The European Court of Justice said on Thursday Belgium's system for levying fines on non-resident commercial vehicle operators is excessive.

A non-resident operator, if stopped in Belgium and found in violation of safety offences agreed under Community regulations, may pay BEF 10,000 for each offence immediately, or BEF 15,000 per offence if the driver wants to challenge the offences and continue criminal prosecution.
If no money is paid, the vehicle may be impounded until the dispute is resolved, at the driver's risk and expense.

In this case, Eckehard Pastoors, a German resident, working for a German company, Trans-Cap GmbH, was stopped in Antwerp and charged with eleven violations. Pastoors consulted his employer and paid the BEF 111,000 immediately.
Trans-Cap and the driver initiated an action against the Belgian state claiming its procedures violate article 6 of the EC Treaty and article 6 of the Convention of Human Rights.
The court said legislation with a greater impact on non-Belgian nationals can be justified by objective circumstances, such as a real risk of unenforceability against the offender.

However, the court found "a national measure ... which requires the payment of such sums, in default of which the vehicle is impounded in the case of non-resident offenders, appears to be excessive ... manifestly disproportionate and thus prohibited by article 6 of the EC treaty."
(Court translation into English. Original language of the case: Dutch)
Reference from the Rechtbank van Eerste Aanleg te Antwerpen (Belgium) for a preliminary ruling in the proceedings between
on the interpretation of article 6 of the EC Treaty and the general principle of equity laid down by Community law

Article 6 of the EC Treaty precludes national legislation adopted in implementation of Council regulation (EEC) No 3820/85 of 20 December 1985 on the harmonization of certain social legislation relating to road transport and of Council regulation (EEC) No 3821/85 of 20 December 1985 on recording equipment in road transport which, in cases of infringement, imposes only on non-residents who opt for continuation of normal criminal proceedings against them rather than for immediate payment of the prescribed fine the obligation to lodge by way of security in respect of each offence a fixed sum higher than that provided for in the case of immediate payment, in default of which their vehicle is impounded.
